title: Destruction's Dangerous Road
description: Destruction's Dangerous Road in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 77, “Are there few that shall he saved?”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: De-struc-tion's dan-gerous road What mul-ti-tudes pur-sue! While that which leads the soul to God, Is known or sought by few.

lines: While that which leads the soul to God,
Is known or sought by few.
But they who will not leave their sin,
They rather choose the way that's wide,
And strive to think it right.
So many surely can't be wrong,
That men will right be found
A few were saved in Noah's ark,
The flock of Christ is always small,
And none are safe but they.
And make them, ere the storm arise,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
